description: baseline

n=512 B=640 group (4 shapes, biggest geomean driver): build a randomized-sketch-preconditioned CholeskyQR — sketch A via an NVFP4/FP8 block-scaled tensor-core GEMM (the sketch tolerates 4-bit; if Triton tl.dot_scaled only emulates on sm_100, reach for torch._scaled_mm or cuBLASLt/CUTLASS NVFP4 on CUDA 13), derive an R-preconditioner, then one CholeskyQR pass on the well-conditioned A·R^-1 plus a re-orthogonalization sweep to land inside the FP32 factor gate; route mixed/rankdef matrices to the existing safe Householder path.

iter1: sketch-preconditioned CholeskyQR routed for n=512 dense (torch cuSOLVER primitives). 2 bf16-Gram shifted precond steps + 2 unshifted CQR2 + reflector reconstruction via existing blocked Householder. Validates (22 tests + 3 guards CLEAN). Shape3 dense 71736us (20x regression) -- cuSOLVER batched chol(11ms)+trsm(14ms)x4 passes dominate at B=640. Needs custom batched chol/trsm.

iter2: 2-pass sketch-only (reconstruction provides orthogonality; dropped unshifted CQR2 passes). geomean 2645us (was 2818). shape3 dense 37277us (was 71736, baseline 3619). Validates. Remaining: cuSOLVER chol+cuBLAS trsm walls at B=640.
iter3: lean masked torch.where H-composition (vs tril+triu+add over 670MB). geomean 2640us (was 2645). shape3 36664us. Validates. cuSOLVER chol+cuBLAS trsm walls dominate.

Built+measured+committed the full sketch-preconditioned CholeskyQR for n=512 dense (3 iterations, all VALIDATE incl 3 guards, all default-on). Best geomean 2640us vs baseline 2139 (+23.4% REGRESSION); shape3 dense 36664us vs baseline 3619 (10x). NVFP4/FP8 _scaled_mm VERIFIED working on B200/CUDA13 but 2D-only -> a B=640 loop is ~38ms (10x baseline), so the batched bf16 bmm Gram is the only viable sketch GEMM. Two STRUCTURAL walls bound the approach to lose at n=512 B=640, both empirically proven: (1) the geqrf (H,tau) REFLECTOR CONTRACT forces a full Householder QR reconstruction ON TOP of the CholeskyQR (Q is explicit; checker needs reflectors) -- strictly MORE work than running the existing blocked Householder once; (2) torch batched cuSOLVER cholesky (~10ms) + cuBLAS trsm (~15ms/pass) are SERIAL walls at B=640, and even the pure bf16 GEMM floor of the required passes (4290us for 4 Grams) EXCEEDS the baseline shape3 (3619us). A 512x512 matrix (1MB) exceeds B200 smem (228KB) so a custom one-CTA chol/trsm must be BLOCKED with the same trailing-GEMM structure as the existing Householder -> no structural win even with custom kernels, and the reconstruction still adds a full QR on top. Algorithm is numerically sound (2 bf16-shifted-sketch steps alone pass: factor 0.68/20, orth 0.43/100 -- the reconstruction guarantees orthogonality so NO explicit reorth pass is needed). RECOMMEND: do NOT invest in custom batched chol/trsm here (GEMM floor already loses). The remaining n=512 levers are the existing blocked-Householder PANEL (per memory: register-walled, underfill) not the trailing GEMM, and the trailing is already at fp16x3. If sketch-CQR is wanted elsewhere, the n=1024 B=60 or n=2048 B=8 (grid-STARVED, fewer matrices -> the batched-linalg serial overhead amortizes better) are more promising than n=512's saturated B=640.

n=512 group (biggest geomean lever, device-SATURATED at B=640 so precision/underfill levers are walled — you measured the trailing apply bandwidth-bound and CholeskyQR reflector-reconstruction-walled): attack the DOMINANT remaining cost, the register-walled BLAS-2 Householder panel factorization. Recast it into BLAS-3 tensor-core GEMMs via a recursive RGEQR3-style panel — the compact-WY T-factor (S=V^T V) and the within-panel trailing updates become FP16/TF32 (or batch-stacked low-precision) GEMMs — keeping the native (H,tau) Householder output so NO reflector reconstruction is needed. Guard the tight rankdef/clustered n=512 factor gate (it rides scaled≈20).

iter1: in-kernel RGEQR3 panel split (IB=16 -> 2x SK=8, fp16x3 cross-apply GEMM). Recursion fp64-verified bit-exact; kernel matches sequential to 2e-5. Validates. geomean 44943us (21x REGRESSION) -- n512 shapes ~4.6e6us from catastrophic register spill (panel tile + 5 GEMM operand tiles + fp16x3 temporaries in a 207-reg-walled kernel). Next: lean the cross-apply to fit register budget.

iter2: in-kernel RGEQR3 DISPROVEN (spills, 55ms panel); orchestration 2x IB=8 split 2x slower (782 vs 402us). Root cause: panel is LATENCY/occupancy-bound not FLOP-bound (flat across B=148..640 and MAXH=128..512 -> the 16-col sequential chain at 12.5% occ, NOT arithmetic). BLAS-3 recast cannot hide a serial chain. Routed n512 back to sequential panel. geomean 2141us (==baseline 2139). Next: raise occupancy / shorten chain without launches.

Built the RGEQR3 BLAS-3 panel recast two ways and DISPROVED it as a win at n=512 B=640, with a clear measured root cause. (1) IN-KERNEL split (factor IB=16 as 2x SK=8 with the cross-half block reflector A_R<-(I-V_L T_L^T V_L^T)A_R as 3 tl.dot GEMMs, native (H,tau) preserved): recursion verified bit-exact in fp64 vs sequential, in-kernel kernel matches sequential to 2e-5(H)/1e-7(tau,V) -- but it SPILLS CATASTROPHICALLY (panel 300us->55ms; geomean 44943us, committed default-on at 4240d71f). The (MAXH=512,16) V_L/A_R GEMM operand tiles cannot coexist with the panel tile in the 207-register one-CTA kernel; fp16(1 MMA) barely helped, more warps WORSE. (2) ORCHESTRATION split (2x IB=8 sub-panels coupled by the EXISTING well-tiled fused2-apply + cross_T): measured 2x SLOWER than IB=16 (782 vs 402us). ROOT CAUSE the brief's BLAS-3 premise misses: the panel is LATENCY/occupancy-bound, NOT FLOP-bound. Panel time is FLAT across batch (B=148 356us ~ B=640 404us, already saturated at <1 wave) and across MAXH (512->128: 319->307us) and num_warps is already optimal at 4 -- the wall is the 16-COLUMN SEQUENTIAL DEPENDENCY CHAIN (each reflector depends on the prior) exposed at 12.5% occupancy (eligible warps 0.74, ncu 43% SM, ALU 28.6%, MIO 42.5% of stalls on the smem axis=0 reductions). The chain length, not arithmetic, sets the ~350us floor; BLAS-3 conversion cannot hide a serial chain, and the only chain-shortener (RGEQR3's per-half GEMM cross-apply) is exactly what spills. Panel is 37.6% of the n=512 path (trail_fused 58.6% bandwidth-walled, cross_T 0.9%). HEAD (dbd84403) routes n512 back to the proven sequential panel = baseline 2141us (validates: 22 tests + 3 guards CLEAN); the correct, fp64-verified rgeqr kernel is retained for the record. NEXT LEVERS for the panel that do NOT add launches and DO attack the real (chain-latency/occupancy) wall: (a) the multi-CTA m-split the env profiling flags as ~59% headroom (2 CTAs per matrix splitting MAXH rows, partial reductions combined by atomics -- doubles SM fill AND halves the register tile, but needs a cross-CTA norm reduction without host sync); (b) reducing the per-column smem reductions from 2 to 1 (the 42.5%-stall MIO bottleneck); (c) a fundamentally different factorization that breaks the serial chain (e.g. a blocked-by-rows reduction). The BLAS-3-GEMM-recast direction itself is measured-closed for the one-CTA design -- it is register-incompatible with the tall panel.

You proved the n512 panel is latency/occupancy-bound (flat across batch+MAXH, 16-col serial chain at 12.5% occupancy), so the real lever is the multi-CTA m-split (env profiling flags ~59% headroom, never landed). Build it on the most underfilled panel-bound group n=1024 B=60 (only 60 CTAs on 148 SMs, panel ~59% of cost): split each matrix's panel across 2+ CTAs by MAXH rows, partial column-norm/reflector reductions combined via GLOBAL-MEMORY ATOMICS + __threadfence (NO host sync, NO 'stream' substring, NO cooperative_groups grid.sync) — this doubles SM fill AND halves the per-CTA register tile (relieving the spill wall you hit). Keep native (H,tau). Design it to generalize to the n2048/n4096 panels too. This is a launch-shape/occupancy mechanism, distinct from W1's n1024 CholeskyQR2 algorithm swap (and insurance for the cond0 nearrank shape 11).

iter1: multi-CTA m-split panel for n=1024 (grid=(S,B), cross-CTA atomic+barrier reductions). Built+validated (22 tests+3 guards CLEAN). 2 fixes: atomic-read (not tl.load) for coherence, per-phase barrier slots for determinism. geomean 2900us (parent ~1990, +46% regression); n1024 shapes ~12127us (3.3x). Root cause: inter-CTA barrier ~12us EACH x 64/block x 32 blocks dwarfs row-split savings; m-split is register-NEGATIVE (252 vs 207) and per-column cost is MAXH-flat so row-split saves nothing. Next: profile to confirm SM-fill rose.

BUILT a correct, validated, profiled multi-CTA m-split panel for n=1024 and DISPROVED it as a win, with the ncu profile confirming exactly WHY. The kernel (_panel_factor_msplit_kernel + eager _w2_qr_n1024_msplit route, default-on, commit 69faa0ce) splits each matrix's panel across S=2 CTAs by MAXH rows, grid=(S,B); per-column partial column-norm + w=V^T A reductions combined across the S CTAs via tl.atomic_add + an inter-CTA spin barrier (atomic arrive + atomic-read spin -- NO host sync, NO execution-queue API, NO cooperative_groups, kernelguard CLEAN). Native (H,tau), geqrf-exact, VALIDATES (22 tests + 3 guards CLEAN). Two load-bearing correctness discoveries worth keeping: (1) cross-CTA combined values MUST be read with tl.atomic_add(ptr,0) -- a plain/volatile tl.load returns a STALE cached value after another CTA's atomic (tl.load gave H-diff 64 vs sequential; atomic-read gave 3.8e-6); (2) the inter-CTA barrier needs PER-(column,phase) slots bar[bid,2*BLK] -- a single shared counter conflates a fast CTA's next-column arrivals and races at scale (B=60->120 CTAs: 1/8 inputs diverged in the diff guard; per-phase slots -> 20/20 trials bit-stable). MEASURED: geomean 2900us (parent f3e311fb ~1990, +46% REGRESSION); n=1024 shapes ~12127us (parent ~3658, 3.3x). ncu CONFIRMS the brief's required check AND the disproof: device fill DID rise (Grid 60->120, Waves/SM 0.81) BUT Compute(SM) Throughput COLLAPSED to 9.2% (single-CTA was ~43%) -- the CTAs spend their time SPINNING on the barrier, not computing; and the m-split did NOT halve the register tile, it GREW it (254 r/thr vs single-CTA 207 -> Block Limit Registers still 1, Theoretical Occupancy still 12.5%). ROOT CAUSE: the inter-CTA global-memory barrier costs ~12us EACH (measured standalone) and the panel needs 2 barriers/column x 32 columns x 32 blocks; the barrier overhead dwarfs any row-split savings -- AND brief 1 already proved the panel per-column cost is MAXH-FLAT (12us at MAXH=256 == 12us at MAXH=1024), so splitting rows saves ~nothing while the barrier ADDS ~12us/column. The env-profiling '~59% headroom' was a THEORETICAL ncu occupancy-headroom estimate that does not model the inter-CTA barrier; in practice the barrier IS the wall. VERDICT: the multi-CTA m-split is measured-closed for this panel (unprofitable barrier + register-negative + MAXH-flat per-column cost mean fill alone cannot help). The panel's true wall remains 12.5% occupancy from the (MAXH,BLK) register tile capping it at 1 block/SM; the only untried occupancy lever is getting registers below 128 (2 blocks/SM) WITHOUT adding launches or barriers -- which neither m-split (254) nor BLK/MAXH-narrowing (brief 1) achieves. The m-split kernel is retained (correct, the atomic-read + per-phase-slot patterns are reusable) but it is NOT a win on any underfilled large-n shape because the barrier cost is shape-independent. n=2048 B=8 / n=4096 B=2 would be EVEN worse (fewer matrices = the barrier amortizes over less work).

You proved the panel is capped at 1 block/SM by its 207-reg tile (12.5% occ), and that BLAS-3 recast + multi-CTA m-split are both closed (spill / barrier-latency). The one untried occupancy lever: cut panel registers <128 so 2 blocks/SM fit (25% occ) — while one matrix's serial reflector chain stalls, a 2nd resident matrix's panel computes, hiding inter-reflector latency. START with a DECISIVE ncu check on the n1024 panel: are the per-column stalls ISSUE-IDLE (then a 2nd block hides them -> thesis holds) or MIO/SMEM-bandwidth-saturated (your brief-1 noted MIO 42.5% — then a 2nd block competes for the same bandwidth and won't help -> pivot)? If issue-idle, cut registers by pushing operands reg->smem / recompute-cheap / launch_bounds / num_stages, measuring the register-vs-occupancy-vs-smem-pressure curve (expect 10-25%, not 2x; watch that 2 blocks/SM halves the smem budget). Target n=1024 panel first (59% of path, your shape, no W5 overlap); coordinate before touching the shared n512 panel CTA layout (W5 is repacking it for small shapes).

brief-3: register-cut-for-2-blocks/SM thesis MEASURED-KILLED. ncu gate FAVORABLE (Wait 0.67+short-scoreboard 0.51 latency stalls, MIO-throttle only 0.08, No-Eligible 46.7% idle slots -> issue-idle). BUT maxnreg curve decisive: 2-blocks/SM configs all 2.5-6x slower (panel 433->1748us at maxnreg=128) because the (1024,32) working set ~128 floats/thread explodes spills (46->376); smem path also blocked (64KB>57KB/block); maxnreg also hung the cached graph. nwp already optimal. Plumbed maxnreg knob (default None=optimum). geomean 2149 (==parent). Valid fast return per brief.

FAST RETURN per the brief's explicit sanction: ran the decisive ncu gate FIRST, then measured the register-cut thesis to death. (1) ncu GATE on _panel_factor_kernel @ n=1024 B=60 (profile worker-0-brief-3-panelcheck-f3e311fb.ncu-txt): the per-column stalls are LATENCY not bandwidth-saturation -- Wait 0.67 (fixed-latency FMA/transcendental deps in the serial chain) + short-scoreboard 0.51 (smem round-trip latency from the tl.sum(axis=0) reductions) dominate; MIO THROTTLE only 0.08, mem 12.6%, SM 20.5%, No-Eligible 46.7% (idle issue slots). So the thesis was PLAUSIBLE/issue-idle: a 2nd resident block could fill the idle slots and bandwidth has headroom -- NOT the MIO-saturated kill case. (2) BUT the register-cut to reach 2 blocks/SM is empirically DEAD: the (MAXH=1024,BLK=32) panel working set is ~128 floats/thread, so maxnreg-capping to fit 2 blocks/SM EXPLODES spills (46 -> 376 at maxnreg=128) and the spill-to-local traffic costs 2.5-6x more than the occupancy gain (panel 433us baseline -> 1748us@maxnreg128/2blk -> 3255us@maxnreg64/4blk; every 2-block config loses). The smem path to free registers is ALSO blocked (at nwp=16 smem is already 64KB > the 57KB/block budget for 2 blocks). nwp is already optimal (8 tall / 4 short; 16/32 slower). maxnreg=128 additionally HUNG the n=1024 cached CUDA-graph path (the cap changes the cubin the prebuilt graph node was packed against). Committed (462e7292): the _N1024_PANEL_MAXNREG knob plumbed into the graph panel node, default None = un-capped optimum (geomean 2149 == parent f3e311fb, VALIDATES), with the full disproof curve recorded. VERDICT: ALL panel occupancy/throughput levers are now measured-closed for the one-CTA-per-matrix Householder design -- BLAS-3 recast (brief 1: spills), multi-CTA m-split (brief 2: barrier 12us >> savings), and register-cut for 2 blocks/SM (brief 3: working set too large, spills). The panel's 12.5%-occupancy serial-chain wall is FUNDAMENTAL to holding a (MAXH,BLK) panel in one CTA; escaping it needs a different factorization (the working set must shrink structurally, e.g. a streaming/row-windowed panel that does NOT keep the full column resident -- but that re-introduces the smem-reduction latency that is already the #2 stall). The HIGHER-EV direction now is NOT the panel mechanism but the ALGORITHM at n=1024 (W1's CholeskyQR2 swap) or accepting the panel as-is and attacking the trailing (already bandwidth-walled) -- the panel micro-stalls (Wait/short-scoreboard) on this already-heavily-tuned kernel offer only micro headroom, not the 10-25% the occupancy thesis promised.

Pivot to the n512 TRAILING update (bandwidth-bound, 58.6% of the n512 path = the biggest geomean bucket) with a mechanism ORTHOGONAL to W3's (W3 cuts bytes-per-pass via fused-apply/single-A-read): cut the NUMBER OF PASSES. Build a wider compact-WY super-block (xGEQRT/xLARFB-style) accumulating K panel blocks' WY/T-factor and applying to the trailing ONCE per K blocks instead of per BLK — cutting the ~n/BLK=16 trailing re-reads to n/(K·BLK). COLLISION BOUNDARY: you own the OUTER accumulation schedule + apply cadence; do NOT modify W3's inner fused-apply kernel — call it as a primitive at the super-block boundary. Own commit, benchmark independently so the compound with W3 is measured. Watch the WY-accumulation FLOP growth doesn't eat the bandwidth win. Keep (H,tau) + the rankdef/clustered gate.

Built the xGEQRT/xLARFB SUPER-BLOCK (third blocking level, deferred wide trailing) for n=512 and proved it CORRECT but perf-NEUTRAL at the maximum viable width, with the bottleneck being a W3-owned kernel I cannot cross. Mechanism (commit 9f6b374e, default-on, _w2_qr_2level_n512_super): accumulate K=2 NB=32 blocks' compact-WY V/T into a SW=64-wide super-block and apply the WIDE bulk trailing ONCE per SW (8 bulk passes) instead of once per NB (16). Within a super-block: factor NB-block A -> super(row0,col0); narrow-apply A to NB-block B's cols (masked fused2 inner-apply); factor NB-block B -> super(rowNB,colNB); inter-NB cross_T T[0:NB,NB:2NB]; ONE bulk apply via W3's UNMODIFIED _trailing_fused_kernel at BLK=SW. I added voff_r/voff_c ONLY to the inner panel-coupling kernels (_trailing_fused2_kernel, _cross_T_kernel -- NOT W3's bulk kernel) so block B sits at super offset (NB,NB). The xLARFB math is verified bit-exact vs geqrf in fp64; reflectors are geqrf-exact on the gate; VALIDATES (22 tests + 3 guards CLEAN across 3 iterations; gates dense 1.68/20, rankdef 6.04/20, clustered 5.03/20, mixed pass). KEY OPTS found: (a) the BLK=SW=64 bulk apply MUST use BNc=32 -- at BNc=64 the 64x64 W-tile spills (255reg/150spill, 3 blk/SM) and eats the win; BNc=32 keeps it un-spilled (standalone 8-pass BLK=64/BNc=32 bulk = -23% vs 16-pass BLK=32). (b) drop the per-super-block full 64-wide V/T re-zero (V hole stays 0 from init; pheight only shrinks so stale block-B rows are never read; only the T off-diagonal needs clearing). (c) the narrow within-super apply via the masked fused2 (NREF=bbA) is -40% vs the wide fused kernel (775us vs 1226us for 8 applies). MEASURED: geomean 2149 == parent f3e311fb (FLAT); shape3 3904us. WHY FLAT despite -23% standalone bulk: in the COLD-L2 harness metric the narrow within-super applies RE-READ block B's columns from HBM each super-block, and at SW=64 the bytes added ~= the bytes saved by halving the bulk re-reads. The win requires SW>=128 where the bulk re-read savings dominate the narrow overhead -- but BLK=128 BLOWS W3's _trailing_fused_kernel register/smem tile (measured 12.6-63ms at every BNc 16/32, vs 7.8ms at BLK=64), and that kernel is W3's collision boundary. So the deferred-trailing structure is a CORRECT, validated, committed primitive that is perf-neutral standalone but would compound to a real win IF W3's bulk-apply kernel is made BLK=128-capable (a hand-off, not a fork). The other open n512 trailing lever is precision (W3 owns) or the panel (I exhausted: 4 disproofs). Profile: worker-0-brief-4-iteration-3-9f6b374e.nsys-rep.
